15	## Introduction
16	
17	Improper storage of hazardous substances may create serious risk, not only to  University  staff  and  students,  but  also  to  emergency  services  personnel, the general public and the environment. The aim of this guidance is to reduce the risk to people's health and to property from the hazards associated with the storage of such substances.
18	
19	This guidance uses transport classification and signage as an aid to explain what  hazards  certain  chemicals  possess,  their  compatibility  and  storage requirements. Transport signage  consists of  diamond  shaped  signs  of differing colours and differing pictograms dependant on the hazard presented by the substance during storage and transport, they are to be found on the external  of  materials  packaged  for  transport  and  in  some  cases  on  the external of vehicles carrying the substances.

These have a white background with a red border and black interior. This style of signage has replaced the old style which had an orange background and contained black pictogram which were replaced in June2015

95	## Risk Assessment
96	
97	A risk  assessment must be carried out for all hazardous substance storage locations. If fire/explosion is the main hazard a risk assessment in compliance with  the  Dangerous  Substances  and  Explosive  Atmospheres  Regulations 2002 (DSEAR) must be undertaken, if the main hazard is release of a toxic, harmful, irritant or corrosive substance then a risk assessment in compliance with the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health 2005 (COSHH) must be undertaken.
98	
99	For the majority of areas storing hazardous substances the following events, both  individually  or  jointly,  have  the  potential  to  cause  significant  harm  or damage and must be considered during the risk assessment process:
100	
101	-  fire;
102	-  explosion;
103	-  release of a toxic substance;
104	-  release of a corrosive substance
105	
106	Heads  of  School/  Support  Units  are  responsible  for  ensuring  that  risk assessments  are  undertaken, significant findings  documented  and  any necessary measures to minimise risk completed. Whilst they cannot transfer responsibility, Heads of School may nominate/delegate sufficient staff to help them  undertake  this.  They  must  ensure  that  these  staff  are  trained  and afforded sufficient time to undertake the risk assessment process.
107	
108	## Information and training
109	
110	Adequate training and knowledge of the properties of hazardous substances is  essential for  their  safe  storage.  All  relevant  staff must  be  informed of  the risks  allied  to  the  storing  of  hazardous  substances,  and  the  precautions necessary  to  safely  store  substances  which  have  different  hazards.  Those responsible for safe storage of hazardous substances need specific training in emergency procedures. Periodic refresher training will normally be required. The training should include the following topics:
111	
112	-  The types of hazardous substances stored, their properties, incompatibilities  and  hazards,  including  hazard  label  recognition  and understanding of the contents of Safety Data Sheets (SDSs);
113	-  General procedures for safe handling;
114	-  Use of protective clothing and respirators;
115	-  Local procedures for dealing with leaks and spillages;
116	-  Housekeeping and record keeping;
117	-  Reporting of faults and incidents, including minor leaks and spills;
118	-  Emergency  procedures,  including  raising  the  alarm  and  the  use  of appropriate fire-fighting equipment.
119	
120	## Labelling of containers
121	
122	Suppliers of hazardous substances must comply with the requirements of the Classification,  Labelling  and  Packaging  of  Substances  and  Mixtures  (CLP Regulation). Compliance ensures that:
123	
124	-  The hazard of the substance has been classified;
125	-  The  substance  is  suitably  labelled  with  both  hazard  pictograms  and specific risk and safety phrases, packaged accordingly; and
126	-  Information, in the form of a Safety Data Sheet (SDS), is available.
127	
128	If  an  SDS is not supplied with the first order of a hazardous substance this should be sought from the supplier who is legally obliged to supply an SDS at no  cost.  In  the  case  of  many  reputable  chemical  suppliers  (e.g.  Fisher Scientific, Sigma Aldrich) the SDS for chemicals that they supply is available online.
129	
130	Containers  containing  hazardous  substances  must  be  clearly  labelled  at  all times. It is especially important to label containers that hazardous substances have  been  decanted  into  with  at  least  the  name  of  the  chemical  and  the white/red  hazard  warning  pictogram.  Hazard  warning  pictogram  labels  are available in differing sizes, to suit container size, from your normal laboratory suppliers.
